goal:
A reviewer asked me to double-check a value from Lindqvist et al. (2025), "Capacity Limits of Polymer Creep" (http://journal-of-alpine-hydrology.example/articles/6c361e-capacity-limits-of-polymer-creep).
What estimated capacity does Table 2 report for station L-08? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.version_label: Version of Record, Journal of Alpine Hydrology (2025)

paragraphs: We study polymer creep across five monitoring stations using a nonparametric model.
Authors: Jonas Lindqvist, Vera Petrenko, Bilal Uchenna. Published in Journal of Alpine Hydrology, 2025.
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report estimated capacity measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional estimated capacity at 2.4 bits/param; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of polymer creep relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station B-04.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Ekstrom et al. (2019). [2] Haldane and Uchenna (2021). [3] Achterberg et al. (2022).
